## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect should be fixed before merge. The new `CRITERION_HINT` gives advice that the still-supported `require_shall=True` validator mode rejects, so anyone who follows the hint with that option on will have every criterion refused. The `BULLET_HINT` rewording matches the `startswith("- ")` check, and no other defects were found in the reviewed scope.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — With `require_shall=True`, a criterion written the way the new hint says, such as `- Save the result`, is rejected. The hint now reads "Write criteria as direct action bullets without the word shall." but `accepts_criterion` still returns `" shall " in text` when `require_shall` is set (`app/criteria.py:7-8`). `tests/test_criteria.py:20-21` confirms that `- Save the result` fails under that option. The pull-request body says it keeps the existing validator options, and `config.example.yml:1` still exposes `require_shall`. One fix is to keep the "without shall" wording only for the default mode and give a separate hint for `require_shall`. Another is to phrase the hint so it doesn't forbid "shall". — When projects set `require_shall: true`, users who follow the displayed hint get every criterion rejected, with no clue that the hint caused it.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `BULLET_HINT` now gives the exact `- ` prefix, which matches the `text.startswith("- ")` check in `app/criteria.py:5`.
- The existing tests (`tests/test_criteria.py`) still cover both `require_shall` modes for bulleted and non-bulleted input, and the change to `app/criteria.py` doesn't touch validator logic.
